provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: In the original orientation, every isolated pixel of colour 4 moves down one row. The floor is a full row of colour 2. If a pixel lands directly above the floor, it splashes a V: two diagonal rays go up-left and up-right until they leave the grid. The factory maps the canonical down vector (1,0) and right vector (0,1) through the D4 transform: an optional column flip, then clockwise rotations, where each rotation sends (dr,dc) to (dc,-dr). From these it gets the visible fall direction and the two ray directions, (-down - right) and (-down + right). The colour roles are fixed as constants: background palette[0], floor palette[2], pixel palette[4]. The emitted program works directly in visible coordinates. It clears every pixel and moves each one one step along the fall direction. A pixel splashes when the next cell in that direction is a floor cell. The splash rays are then drawn in pixel colour, clipped at the grid border. Pixels on the far side of the floor simply move one step and never splash, because the cell after them is never floor. Rectangular grids and every D4 orientation are handled by the vector constants alone.
draft_notes.limitations: The program assumes the constructor's domain. Pixels never start on the floor or directly before it, and never fall off the grid. Outputs never collide, since the generator rejects overlapping draws, so there are no tie-breaks. For out-of-domain inputs, a pixel that would move onto the floor or off the grid stays where it is; this is only a defensive choice. Colour roles are taken from the palette constants rather than inferred from the demonstrations. The fixtures are consistent with the uniform rule, and I found no constructor defects. This code has not been run or tested.
